newsitem.title: BURMA: Unocal president meets Burma's Aung San Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Unocal president meets Burma's Aung San Suu Kyi.

text.p: The president of Unocal Corp, the biggest U.S. investor in Burma, met Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi at her residence in central Rangoon, a government statement said on Saturday.
The defence ministry statement declined to say what John Imle discussed with the Burmese opposition leader during their nearly one-hour meeting on Friday at her house on University Avenue.

The U.S.-based oil company has been condemned by human rights groups for ignoring their calls for international sanctions against Burma's ruling military government, the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
Suu Kyi has also called for economic sanctions against Burma as part of international pressure for the SLORC to ease its restrictions on opposition activities in the country.
Unocal chief executive Roger Beach said last month he was disappointed by unilateral U.S. economic sanctions against Burma.
The company has said it does not expect that U.S. sanctions would affect its current $1.2 billion natural gas project in Burma, although it will hit its future involvement in the country.

Unocal has a 28 percent stake in the offshore Yadana gas project, which is operated by France's Total Petroleum. The other partners are Thailand's PTTEP and Burmese state-controlled Myanmar Oil and Gas Enterprise (MOGE).
University Avenue has been barricaded around Suu Kyi's house since late last year to prevent people from visiting her.
